metadata.title: Nova × Monroe × Vieira convergence matrix
metadata.rule: Independent or semi-independent vocabularies mapping toward the same NC node identify comparison targets, not proof of the phenomenon's mechanism or ontology.

clusters.shared_minimum_description: A subjectively perceived internal or body-wide vibration/electric/oscillatory condition occurring around altered-state or separation-oriented transitions.
clusters.theoretical_divergence: Gateway embeds the cue in nonphysical-energy training language; Projectiology explains it through energossoma/psychosome dynamics; Nova keeps the canonical node at the level of reported vibration phenomenology and transition context.
clusters.evidence_note: Strong lexical and phenomenological convergence across two external traditions, but agreement does not independently validate either energetic explanation.

clusters.shared_minimum_description: A transition away from ordinary bodily localization toward a separation-like or displaced-point-of-view condition, distinguished from the later destination or outcome.
clusters.theoretical_divergence: Gateway commonly describes physical/nonphysical energies or second-body separation; Projectiology names psychosome takeoff; Nova formalizes a perceptual/self-location transition without requiring either external vehicle ontology.
clusters.evidence_note: The cross-tradition overlap is strongest at the transition-structure level, not at the level of what is claimed to separate.

clusters.shared_minimum_description: An incomplete separation-like configuration in which only part of the experienced body representation is displaced or free before a possible more complete transition.
clusters.theoretical_divergence: Gateway's Pole method instructs a staged second-body maneuver; Projectiology interprets semiprojection as partial psychosome exteriorization; Nova records incomplete exit-like body phenomenology without committing to a vehicle ontology.
clusters.evidence_note: Especially useful for structured reports because the partial-body pattern is concrete enough to compare without accepting either external mechanism.

clusters.shared_minimum_description: Deliberately induce, amplify or use axial/whole-body rotation as a maneuver intended to support a separation transition.
clusters.theoretical_divergence: Both external alignments currently come from Gateway, so this is procedural redundancy inside one tradition rather than cross-tradition convergence.
clusters.evidence_note: Strong operational match, but it should not be counted as two independent traditions.

clusters.shared_minimum_description: A floating, rising, gliding or suspended-body sensation that may be spontaneous or deliberately evoked during transition-oriented practice.
clusters.theoretical_divergence: Gateway techniques interpret the cue inside its energy-body training model; Nova separates the floating phenomenon from Décrochage and does not treat it as proof of actual separation.
clusters.evidence_note: Useful as a cue/induction cluster, but only one external tradition is currently represented.

clusters.shared_minimum_description: Temporary inability to move the physical body while awareness is present around a sleep/transition state.
clusters.theoretical_divergence: Projectiology adds a vehicle-coincidence explanation; Nova records the immobility/awareness phenomenon without adopting that mechanism.
clusters.evidence_note: Gateway manuals also mention temporary stiffness/immobility in separation practice, but no dedicated Gateway concept has yet been formalized for this node, so it is not counted as a second external alignment.

clusters.shared_minimum_description: Experience or representation of a body-like form distinct from ordinary physical-body ownership or localization.
clusters.theoretical_divergence: Nova explicitly defines Corps de sortie as a perception and not ontological proof; Projectiology treats Psicossoma as a real vehicle of manifestation within its framework.
clusters.evidence_note: The low-confidence partial overlap is scientifically useful precisely because the two systems diverge sharply on ontology.

clusters.shared_minimum_description: Maintain awareness while reducing effort, expectation-monitoring or active interference once the transition process is underway.
clusters.theoretical_divergence: The operational strategy can be compared independently of Gateway's energy-body interpretation or Nova's internal transition vocabulary.
clusters.evidence_note: The Freedom source-claim layer independently repeats relaxed practice without expectations, but because it belongs to the same Gateway tradition it is not counted as another tradition.
